Quantum entanglement remains a counterintuitive phenomenon in modern physics, challenging assumptions about locality and realism. Entangled particle states are inextricably linked such that measuring one instantly dictates the state of the other regardless of distance. Loophole-free tests consistently violated Bell inequalities, proving non-locality at the quantum scale. The collapse of the Roman Republic was a prolonged erosion of institutional norms that began decades before Julius Caesar crossed the Rubicon. Client-patron networks transformed into competitive instruments of political warfare. Patricians accumulated vast agricultural estates worked by enslaved labor, driving plebeian farmers into urban landlessness dependent on political benefactors.
